newsitem.title: GHANA: Think-tank says Ghana inflation may pick up.
newsitem.headline: Think-tank says Ghana inflation may pick up.

text.p: A Ghanaian think-tank has warned that the West African nation's inflation rate, which halved in 1996 to an estimated 35 percent, might surge again.
The Centre for Policy Analysis (CEPA), led by former finance minister Joe Abbey, said in a report published on Tuesday that factors that brought inflation down in 1996 may not prove sustainable.
"All these factors must be set against the continued deterioration in the fundamentals," the centre said in its Macroeconomic Review for Q3 1996, published on Tuesday.
"Some of them, including the statistical element, are not only unsustainable but could work in reverse and produce a resurgence in inflation sooner or later," it added.
Year-on-year inflation fell in 1996 from 70 percent in December 1995 to an estimated 35 percent in December 1996.
The Centre attributed this to good harvests in 1995 and 1996, artificially low petroleum prices, Central Bank support of the cedi and restraint on the part of trade unions.
A statistical "bonus", stemming from a 1995 inflation surge following the chaotic introduction of Value Added Tax, also helped the 1996 figure, the centre said.
President Jerry Rawlings, reelected in December, told parliament last week the government aimed to bring inflation below 10 percent within 18 months.
But the Centre said government macro-economic policy was resulting in money supply growth, large budget deficits and current account and overall balance of payment deficits.
Abbey is a member of the board of directors of Bank of Ghana, the central bank.
